reviews.text: [h1]终于忙完了，什么！你说还有十单？！[/h1] [h2]游戏介绍[/h2] 《哥布林寿司》是由Old Fake Factory工作室开发，Metaroot发行的一款结合了roguelike和餐厅模拟经营的瑞士独立游戏，你将在游戏中扮演一名哥布林寿司厨师，为各种口味挑剔的客人做出满足他们口味的寿司，为付出一轮又一轮房租做出努力。 [h2]游戏玩法-手忙脚乱的工作现场[/h2] 游戏主要是采用了roguelike类玩法，在一轮又一轮上菜的过程中提升等级，并选择你需要的效果，可以说新型寿司，也可以是其他加钱效果，比如让顾客吃完后把盘子也吃了，这样就不用自己去收拾，在后期制作复杂，人数众多的情况可以有效缓解杂乱的现场。我刚开始游玩时觉得这游戏十分简单，有点像小孩玩的益智游戏，但后面我选择了新菜品后，突然发现有点跟不上游戏节奏，由于不熟悉新型寿司的菜谱，我老是放错材料导致给顾客送上了便便（没错，字面意思），然后喜提差评，还要忙中偷偷补货，一个成语概括就是手忙脚乱，可能是我玩的还不够熟练，总之熟练之后会有一种云淡风轻的感觉，像是自己的店真做出了一番成绩。 [h2]游戏总结[/h2] 总体评分8.9/10吧，在同类游戏中还挺有趣的，哥布林这个主题也很有意思，很无厘头，你想挑战手速可以尝试这游戏。 [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45753062/]来和我组乐队吧~ [/url] 凡游皆如乐，步履扣心弦。 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url= https://steamcommunity.com/groups/mygoreview] →‘一键组乐队’←[/url] 轻拢复慢捻，共度忘华年。 [/quote]

There's a playable game here, but it's undercooked. It looks and sounds like an old flash game from the 2000s, but if you played many of those, remember that there were plenty of rancid shovelware-tier ones. Even the good ones were often merely enjoyable because they were **free** and sort of portable, being playable on nearly any PC with an internet connection. The sound design in particular is pretty bad, in my opinion. Some things you'd expect to have sounds (like the landlord exploding upon a win) simply don't. The sounds you do hear are either pretty generic or actively unpleasant-- in particular, the customers. Every single one makes the same pitched-up annoying "numnumnum" on eating or an obnoxious, childish growl if they don't get their food fast enough, which can happen often due to the food being served on a conveyer belt (meaning it might be eaten too fast by customers on the left side, although you have some ways to influence this). Maybe giving the various customers specific sound queues in addition to gameplay quirks (like the one that eats poop) would really benefit the experience. It's not actively bad, visually, although the customers all grow and shrink excessively in some kind of awkward "breathing" pseudo-animation. Each one has a sprite for idling, eating, and getting impatient, which is good enough. I do love the giant goblin+baby army boss. Gameplay-wise, it's as unpolished as you'd expect from a fresh Early Access roguelike, but to be fair, I could only see so much within 2 hours and the two easiest difficulty levels. Get a broken combo of upgrades and spam what works. The only ingredient type that doesn't reward spamming out as many as possible is grilled, because it spoils into poop, but you can get upgrades to allow you to spam poop and win in a very lazy way. It's neat that that strategy exists, but there are other upgrades like Omakase! (customers have a chance to buy and eat anything they see instead of their desired order) and one or two that convince regular customers to sometimes eat poop, allowing you to almost completely ignore the game's mechanics and just dump whatever scores high on the sushi belt as fast as possible. Maybe additional recipes should somehow get pushed into the player's inventory instead of being part of the upgrade pool-- it seems like the game really rewards specializing into a very generic menu, which gets boring, fast. Maybe higher difficulties fix this, but I'd need more time to see if that's the case. For now, I'm refunding; the asking price is too high for the current quality (and I can't stand "supporter packs" that have in-game content!). That being said, I'll keep Goblin Sushi on my wishlist and see how it develops; there's a chance it'll grow into something worth the price tag (and/or go on a steep sale) later on.

Update June 2026: So after some updates i thought to try it again and see if it became more complex and challenging. It got a tad bit more challenging but still not a lot. I did two more runs and i beat second difficulty first try, third difficulty second try, but i wasnt tryharding at all. I like the new perks etc, but overall it didnt get enough variation or stuff to keep me playing. Endless Mode is pointless because i scaled so strong that i couldnt even pick any more upgrades. Theres also not a lot to do in this kitchen, its all pretty basic and im not seeing the major differences between the first kitchen and the second water based one. I couldnt even tell whats missing here. But to me it seems like the basic formula works well, but is still lacking something to make it fun. Whether its the dishes being too sub complex or the customers being too sub complex, i dont know. Maybe i need more cooking minigames to be busy, maybe perks feel too strong and onesided. I cant tell. But it feels a lot like a Mobile Game, so i wasnt really surprised to see it is one. What i might like to see: More modes with challenges, more complex gadgets, gadget meta progression instead of purchasing perks (like leveling/improving my rice cooker), more substantial and interesting perks, that dont outright eliminate gameplay elements. Tried it and went through it pretty easily. I didnt reach max difficulty in my playtime, but went through the first two with only doing the same dish constantly and maximizing my buffs. I already kind of saw everything it had to offer and it wasnt yet enough to keep me engaged. It def. needs more motivation to learn new recipes, needs more buff variants and maybe ways to customize your menu. Also more different guest types with different needs and varied expectations, as well as proper meta progression OR kitchen customization where i can give the whole thing my own touch, focus and twist (like for example turning the grill into a big one plate grill or add more rice cookers, change arrangements or something like that). Not just visually. What could probably be the nest thing ever was a coop mode, basically like Galaxy Burger or Cook Serve Delicious, where you manage a bigger kitchen and a longer conveyor belt together. Then this would be an instant buy for us even while flawed. Maybe also more ways to spend money, as i had plenty to waste and nothing really to do with. Which is where you could bring in Meta currency, so during my run i can convert my money into meta currency at the risk of losing if i convert too much. I will check back later when it received some more updates.

This is not actually a cooking game, or at least, it's a very weird cooking game where you have to pick out 'perks' which combine well together and just serve dishes fast. It doesn't need you to keep track of customers and their favorites, or feed them the correct meals to unlock their stories and progress further into friendship. You are limited to 5 recipes (but they can be different every run) and are expected to replay the game multiple times. I think the point is to earn more money each time than you did before? Genuinely not sure how you win at this game since even if you blow up the landlord and the game ends with a 'win', your progress is still not completely unlocked. I am enjoying this game but it's a very confusing experience.

Really fun game with a satisfying progression curve. Worth the price if you're the kind of person who likes exploring various builds and combos in roguelite games. Some builds are ridiculously overpowered compared to others which can be a downside or make for a fun challenge depending on how you look at it. Overall I would still like the game to be a bit more balanced. Otherwise the art is neat, the music is alright and the story (if you can call it that) adds a layer of humour without being intrusive. The only real issue I have with this game is the lack of option to rebind keyboard shortcuts. The new level has been a pleasant surprise. I expected minor differences but overall similar recipes and combos, and clearly underestimated the devs. It's different enough that I had to spend a couple runs finding my footing playing the hardest difficulty mode. If the devs keep adding levels without raising the price or shipping them as dlc, I'll probably consider buying the supporter pack.

经典的料理游戏融合了随机地牢机制。极快的游戏节奏激发了大量的多巴胺。 游戏的主要目标是在单局游戏里，达成约十轮的分数提交。每一轮的扣分阶段之后可以使用多余分数进行加成购买或加成删除，打造自己的料理方式。通过料理的随机组合和加成选择能打造令人愉悦的大分数奇景。在忙碌的快手料理之外，也有通过其他方式打造精品菜肴获得大分数的可能。 当前的游戏还处于开发阶段，在内容丰富度上还有一定的欠缺。 不足： 1，只有两张风格迥异的地图； 2.一些套路相似而固定； 3.不同料理体系间缺乏联动，小吃更多的时候只是为了暂时降低对主资源的占用，不容易转变成分数主力； 4.一些成就要求过于繁琐，又与开局解锁项挂钩。

[quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/6142328/][b] With 1,500+ reviews, please consider following The Cpt Froggy Club Curator Page for plenty more![/b][/url][/quote] Goblin Sushi: ~~~~~~~~~~ Did you know that Sushi was a high-end restaurant experience in America back in the 1960s? Believe it or not, a special Sushi roll back then cost around $3 to $5, which is equivalent to $30 to $50 in today's money. I can't recall having ever seen a Japanese restaurant when I was growing up in Geneva in the 70s or 80s. My first Sushi experience was around the mid-2000s, a whopping ten years after I touched down in the land Down Under. And let me tell you, I could stuff my face with Sushi like there was no tomorrow at my local Sushi train for $50 those days. But the boom of Japanese cuisine has grown so much that even imaginary beings are craving it! It's the turn of the Goblin world to be flooded with slices of raw fish on top of beds of rice. And you, my friend, you are the chef who will make it happen, in Goblin Sushi! Goblin Sushi is a casual cooking job simulator with roguelike and deck-building elements, developed by Old Cake Factory and published by Metaroot on the 10th of February 2026 on the Steam platform. At the time I am writing this review, the game is in early access, and the gameplay and content might change when it reaches version 1.0. So what do you have to do? In a nutshell, you must manage to pay your greedy landlord rent eleven times in a row, to the point of making him explode with his cash. But achieving this will be quite a task. After all, you'll be preparing the food, serving it, cleaning the plates when your patrons finish their meals, and making sure you have enough ingredients for the entire run. Now, I haven't been able to unlock the second level so far. I'm about 40% off the mark after 10 hours of gameplay, which is pretty good. But essentially, you have the workstation in front of you, with a mixer on the left to make the juices. Next to it are the ingredient containers, which you need to keep as full as possible. The sush mat is next to the containers, and on the right-hand side will be your grill, which also has three ingredient containers next to it. And on the far right is the recipe book, in case you forget how the dishes you are offering your patrons are made. I believe the second level differs in terms of the workstation, ingredients, and recipes. Is it going to be hectic? Not for the first two payments, but after that, you'd wish you were born with a few pairs of arms, that's for sure. The run will start with the same recipe (in level one), which is the Onigiri (rice and seaweed). Customers will start appearing at your workstation with their orders. The maximum number of customers you'll have at any given time is four, at least on the first level; after that, I can't tell. After placing their order, which is an image of the recipe, you'll notice a gauge next to it. This gauge starts depleting the moment the order is placed, and you have to serve the dish to the customer before it's completely depleted. If you don't, the client will be angry and leave, not tipping you. It will also affect your star rating, which in turn will affect the client's overall tips. So the goal is to keep serving the right dish on time, clear plates, and keep turning order after order. Remember, your landlord will keep raising the rent whenever he wants his money. So, you have to go faster and faster to keep up with his demand. It will become very tricky, especially when you have recipes with up to 9 ingredients to make with your Sushi mat, as well as dishes that require cooking on the grill! It will become a mad Sushi house! But that's not all! As you serve the correct dishes on time, not only do you get paid for your hard work, but you'll also receive experience points. The XP gauge is at the top of your screen, and when it is full, you'll be prompted to choose from one of three cards that will pop up on your screen. Take your time before selecting one, because it will determine whether you have a losing or a winning run. For example, you might have a card that increases the speed of the Shusi mat. If the last ingredient placed on the mat is seaweed, it might double your XP each time a dish is consumed. It increases the price of a dish or gives you a new dish to serve your goblin patrons. There are nearly 200 cards, giving you plenty of variations that make each run a bit different from the others. Oh, I nearly forgot to mention that odd goblin characters will turn up too, such as the goblin devils who can offer things with a string attached, or the salesman who is happy to sell your perk (cards), tough choices, let me tell you. But there is one thing that has bugged me since I started playing this game. There is no guidance on how to unlock things, as you don't have a Gamepedia available to you. Sure, it will tell you at the end of the run that you unlocked a new feature, because you served a specific dish for X amount of time. But because there is no guidance on what to do next, you have no idea how to unlock something else and move up to the next level, which is annoying. The graphics are fun, the game in itself is surprisingly addictive and has a couple of levels of difficulty. The sound the goblins make after consuming their meals is very similar to the sound of the martians in the movie Mars Attacks! Cracked me up every time, knap knap knap! lol. Positives: ~~~~~~~ + Fun graphics and music + Nearly 200 cards to select from + Good selection of Japanese dishes + Fun, chaotic and addictive gameplay + Each run is slightly different + A few levels of difficulty + Achievements Negatives: ~~~~~~~~ - It is a bit repetitive - Need a gamepedia and guidance on how to unlock things - No trading cards as yet Goblin Sushi is a fun and addictive cooking game. A Gamepedia and some guidance on how to unlock things would elevate it. 7/10 Note: Key provided directly by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!
